A_target.statement:
There is no set $R$ whose members are exactly the sets which are not members of themselves.
Consequently naive comprehension is inconsistent, and in the presence of the [[Axiom of Specification]] there is no set of all sets.

B_source.statement:
Let $f: S \to \powerset S$.
Then $D = \set {x \in S: x \notin \map f x}$ is not in the image of $f$.
This is [[Cantor's Theorem]].

substitutions.the map f: x -> x, each set viewed as the collection of its members

object_map.reformulation: Run Cantor's diagonal argument with the map sending each set to itself.

validity_conditions: The argument only needs that R would be one of the sets x considered.
With specification, a universal set V would yield R = {x in V : x not in x}.
proof_plan: Apply the diagonal construction to the map $x \mapsto x$: the diagonal set is $\set {x: x \notin x} = R$.
Then $R \in R \iff R \notin R$, a contradiction.
